svg.text: READING GUIDE | ER TO RELATIONAL SCHEMA
Companion to the conceptual Chen diagram — keep this off the main presentation slide.

g.text: Why six entities but seven database tables?
WATCHLIST — CONTAINS — INSTRUMENT is a many-to-many relationship.
The relationship attribute added_at records when membership was created.
Relational mapping produces watchlist_items(watchlist_id, instrument_id, added_at).
Composite PK: (watchlist_id, instrument_id); both columns reference parent tables.
Cardinality and participation are different
1:N means one parent can relate to many children; it does NOT mean at least one.
Every WATCHLIST belongs to a USER: total participation at WATCHLIST.
A USER may have zero watchlists: partial participation at USER.
An empty watchlist is permitted, and an instrument need not be on any watchlist:
CONTAINS remains partial on BOTH sides.
Candidate keys and alternate uniqueness (from the implemented schema)
USER PK user_id; alternate keys username and email (each individually UNIQUE).
INSTRUMENT PK instrument_id; alternate key (exchange, symbol) as one composite UNIQUE.
WATCHLIST PK watchlist_id; alternate key (user_id, name).
PRICE_TICK PK tick_id; alternate key (source, instrument_id, source_event_id).
ALERT_RULE PK rule_id; alternate key (user_id, instrument_id, direction, threshold).
ALERT_EVENT PK event_id; alternate key (rule_id, tick_id).
In conceptual Chen notation, a key containing a relationship is clarified here, not drawn as a copied FK.
Integrity rule: scope of database enforcement
For each ALERT_EVENT, its ALERT_RULE and PRICE_TICK must refer to the same INSTRUMENT.
The described event trigger checks this on INSERT or UPDATE of rule_id / tick_id.
The current trigger does NOT prevent later instrument_id changes on parent records.
Verified: PostgreSQL accepts such UPDATEs on alert_rules and price_ticks.
The rule holds in practice only because no application path changes instrument_id.
Do not add an extra relationship diamond just to represent this cross-table rule.
Presenting the diagram to faculty
Conceptual ER: entities, attributes, relationships, cardinality and participation.
Relational schema: seven physical tables, keys, FKs, data types and ON DELETE.
Composite “listing” groups exchange and symbol; it is NOT a stored SQL column.
ALERT_EVENT is an entity because it records an occurrence with event_id/fired_at.
The M:N CONTAINS relationship becomes the watchlist_items junction table.
Quick notation reminder
Rectangle = entity • Oval = attribute • Diamond = relationship • Underline = key
1 / N / M = cardinality at each relationship end • Double connector = total participation
No arrowheads, no SQL types, no FK columns copied merely to redraw relationship lines.
